report.source_text: After consultation with the oncology team, long-acting octreotide 30 mg monthly was suggested. The patient was discharged, but a few days later, he complained from perioral, hand, and feet paresthesia and numbness and developed symptomatic hypocalcemia; his corrected calcium level was 6.5 mg/dl, phosphate level was 2.5 mg/dl, 25 hydroxy vitamin D level was 22.8 ng/ml, and the PTH level was 107 pg/ml. He received intravenous and oral calcium accompanied by 50,000 units of oral ergocalciferol weekly. The symptoms were relieved, and the calcium level was corrected

clinician.final_diagnosis: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low grade) of the liver confirmed by percutaneous biopsy with immunohistochemistry showing strongly positive chromogranin and synaptophysin, negative CK20, CK7, LCA, and Ki-67 index <3%
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old Iranian man presented with acute constitutional symptoms (nausea, vomiting, generalized headache, malaise, and 13 kg weight loss over 1 month) and severe hypercalcemia (>15 mg/dL) with suppressed PTH (4.37 pg/mL), low vitamin D (14 nmol/L), and acute kidney injury (creatinine 4.12 mg/dL, BUN 47 mg/dL). CT imaging of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed a 51×47 mm heterogeneous solid mass in the pancreatic body with calcification and multiple hypodense lesions in the liver (largest 73×67 mm in left lobe with calcification). Percutaneous biopsy of the liver mass was performed and histopathology confirmed a well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low grade) with strongly positive chromogranin and synaptophysin immunostaining, negative CK20, CK7, and LCA, and Ki-67 index <3%. The severe hypercalcemia was managed with normal saline infusion, calcitonin, hemodialysis, and denosumab, with calcium levels decreasing from >26 mg/dL to 11.9 mg/dL. After diagnosis confirmation, the patient was treated with long-acting octreotide 30 mg monthly and everolimus 10 mg daily. Hemi-pancreatectomy and liver transplantation were recommended by the transplant surgeon but refused by the patient and family. Post-discharge, the patient developed symptomatic hypocalcemia (corrected calcium 6.5 mg/dL) with perioral, hand, and feet paresthesia and numbness, which was managed with intravenous and oral calcium supplementation and ergocalciferol, with symptom relief and calcium level correction.
